I don’t have live‑internet access, so I can’t pull up the very latest headlines for you right now. However, I can show you how to get recent stock news yourself (or how you could build a small script that does it). Below are a few common ways to retrieve news for a particular ticker:

| Method | What you’ll need | How it works |
|--------|------------------|--------------|
| **Yahoo Finance RSS** | `https://finance.yahoo.com/rss/headline?s=MSFT` | Just hit the URL for the ticker’s RSS feed; parse the XML. |
| **Alpha Vantage News API** | API key from Alpha Vantage | Call `https://www.alphavantage.co/query?function=NEWS_SENTIMENT&tickers=MSFT&apikey=YOUR_KEY`. |
| **Finnhub.io News API** | API key from Finnhub | Call `https://finnhub.io/api/v1/company-news?symbol=AAPL&from=2024-01-01&to=2024-12-31&token=YOUR_TOKEN`. |
| **NewsAPI.org** | API key from NewsAPI | Search for “Microsoft” or “AAPL” with `q=Microsoft&apiKey=YOUR_KEY`. |
| **Python libraries** | `requests`, `feedparser`, `pandas` | Use them to fetch and parse the feeds/APIs above. |

### Quick Python example (using `requests` + `feedparser`)

```python
import requests
import feedparser

def get_yahoo_rss(ticker):
    url = f"https://finance.yahoo.com/rss/headline?s={ticker}"
    resp = requests.get(url)
    if resp.status_code != 200:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to fetch RSS: {resp.status_code}")
    feed = feedparser.parse(resp.content)
    return [(entry.title, entry.link) for entry in feed.entries]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ticker = "AAPL"
    news_items = get_yahoo_rss(ticker)
    for title, link in news_items[:5]:
        print(title)
        print(link)
        print("-" * 80)
```

This will give you the top five headline titles and links for Apple. You can adapt the same idea for other tickers or switch to an official API if you need more structured data (e.g., timestamps, sentiment scores).

---

#### If you’re looking for a quick manual check

1. Go to [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/).
2. Type the ticker (e.g., `MSFT`) into the search bar.
3. Click on the “News” tab – you’ll see the most recent articles.

---

Let me know if you’d like help setting up a specific API call, parsing the results into a DataFrame, or anything else!
